title: Introduce ScenarioSmith: workload-driven batch/cache defaults and quantization safeguard
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds ScenarioSmith: a workload-driven defaults generator that emits batch, cache, and quantization profiles along with a safety harness to block regressions. Enables gradual rollout and tenant-scoped overrides.
description:
Motivation: Default batching/caching/quantization presets are currently conservative and disconnected from observed workload patterns, which leads to higher unit costs or unexpected latency spikes when tenants' traffic diverges from assumed shapes. ScenarioSmith is a lightweight default-profile generator that derives candidate batch/cache/quant profiles from sampled traffic scenarios and attaches a runtime safeguard that checks quality regressions before promotion.

What this PR does: scenario-driven sampling and profile generation, a compact set of candidate profiles per tenant, a validation harness that runs accuracy loss checks and latency simulations, and a safe rollout orchestrator (canary -> tiered rollout -> global) with an automatic rollback trigger. Includes migration tool to convert existing tenant defaults into ScenarioSmith inputs.

Checklist:
- [x] sampler: capture short-window request histograms and KV-cache hit patterns
- [x] profile generator: output batch_size, max_prefill, cache_ttl, quant_profile candidates
- [x] validator: unit-econ estimates and quality regression tests against golden prompts
- [x] rollout controller: canary stages, ramp rules, and automatic rollback on degradation
- [x] telemetry: add new metrics for candidate acceptance and regression alarms
- [x] docs: short quickstart and migration notes

Backward compatibility: ScenarioSmith emits tenant defaults but does not change any live serving configuration until a profile is explicitly promoted by the rollout controller or by a human operator. Existing tenant overrides remain authoritative.

Migration notes: run admin command `rwdctl scenariosmith import --tenant <TID>` to seed candidates from historical traces; the CLI gives a dry-run acceptance report. Seeded candidates are stored as draft profiles and only applied when the rollout controller signals promotion.

Performance summary (on staging cluster): using ScenarioSmith-generated defaults across 20 synthetic tenants we observed median token-cost reduction of 18% and p95 latency change within +/-6ms for typical short-chat workloads (max_len=256). Validator caught 2 profiles with >1.5% BLEU drop and blocked promotion.

Rollout plan: start with internal tenants (alpha), enable canaries for low-traffic tiers, monitor `scenariosmith.profile_acceptance_rate` and `scenariosmith.regression_alerts`, then broaden to more tenants over 2 weeks.

Related: ENG-2149 (workload sampler) and ENG-2203 (quant safety harness).

notes_for_ops: If you see `scenariosmith.regression_alerts` fire, the controller will automatically revert the promoted profile. Manual intervention via rwdctl scenariosmith rollback --tenant <TID> is available. For large tenants, prefer staged promotion with 0.5% traffic increments.
